prompt:
The head chef signs the ageing cabinet off every Monday before service, so the door is left shut and the check photograph is taken straight through the glass.

Three bone-in ribs hang on their own hooks inside the cabinet, and every hook carries a spring balance with a dial face. The tag wired to each rib is printed with the date it went in and the weight it went in at: 22 February at 7.2 kilograms, 8 February at 10.0 kilograms, 25 January at 6.4 kilograms. The loss chart taped to the inside of the door reads: after a fortnight 0.92 of the weight is left, after four weeks 0.84, after six weeks 0.74. The docket clipped to the handle dates this check 8 March, and the cabinet air stands at 1 degree and 82 per cent.

What each balance ought to be showing this morning is what the tags do not say.
easy_question: Does this picture show a glass-fronted ageing cabinet with joints of beef hanging inside on hooks, each hook carrying a spring balance? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Three tags hang in the cabinet, each printed with a date. Find the rib whose tag is printed 25 January and read the dial of the spring balance on that hook. Give the reading in kilograms.
Read the dial of the spring balance on the hook whose tag is printed 8 February, and write down that reading.
Now read the dial of the spring balance on the hook whose tag is printed 22 February, and write down that reading.
Read the weight printed on the tag itself that is dated 8 February, and write down that figure.
